title: Jetts vs Float Well NZ – Which Gym or Wellness Centre Is Right for You?
meta_desc: Compare Jetts NZ and Float Well NZ on price, contract, facilities, 24/7 access and overall value. Find the best fit for flexibility, recovery or budget.
intro: Both Jetts and Float Well operate in selected New Zealand cities, but they cater to very different needs. Jetts is a low‑cost, no‑lock‑in gym, while Float Well is a boutique recovery studio offering float tanks, sauna and cold plunge. This guide breaks down the key differences so you can pick the right option for your goals and budget.

sections.heading: Brand at a Glance
sections.body: Jetts NZ positions itself as a budget‑friendly, 24/7 gym with no joining fee and no long‑term contract. It offers basic strength equipment, free weights and parking, making it a solid choice for members who want flexibility and a straightforward workout space. Float Well NZ, on the other hand, is a boutique wellness centre focused on recovery therapies – floatation tanks, an infrared sauna and a cold plunge. It does not provide traditional gym equipment or group classes, but it excels at stress relief, sleep improvement and post‑exercise recovery.
list: Jetts – 24/7 access, basic gym equipment, no lock‑in
Float Well – float tanks, infrared sauna, cold plunge, no gym equipment

sections.heading: Price, Contracts & Cancellation
sections.body: Jetts charges $14.95–$19.95 per week depending on the city and whether you opt for the standard or premium package. There is no joining fee and no contract – you can cancel at any time with a 14‑day notice. Float Well’s pricing starts at $25.00 per week for a basic membership that includes unlimited float sessions and sauna access; premium tiers go up to $80.00 per week for added contrast therapy and guest passes. Both brands advertise $0 joining fees, but Float Well requires advance booking for each session. Eligible New Zealanders may qualify for the Exercise NZ subsidy, which can reduce the weekly cost by 40–70 % for either provider, subject to eligibility criteria.

rows: No contract, cancel anytime; booking required per session

sections.heading: Facilities & Services
sections.body: Jetts delivers the essentials for a functional workout: free weights, cardio machines, a small selection of resistance equipment and 24/7 access. Personal training is available at an extra cost, but there are no group classes or specialised recovery zones. Float Well offers a completely different suite – a 500 kg Epsom‑salt float tank, an infrared sauna heated to 70 °C, and a cold plunge kept at 7–8 °C. Guest passes are included in higher tiers, and the centre provides a quiet, meditative environment ideal for athletes seeking post‑training recovery. However, you won’t find any dumbbells or squat racks at Float Well.
list: Jetts – basic gym floor, optional PT, parking
Float Well – float tank, infrared sauna, cold plunge, limited gym equipment

sections.heading: Locations & 24/7 Access
sections.body: Jetts operates in selected cities across New Zealand, with a focus on suburban strips and shopping centre locations. Its 24/7 model means you can work out any time, and most sites provide free parking. Float Well is currently limited to a flagship centre in Wellington’s CBD, with plans for a second site pending. Access is by appointment only during opening hours (typically 7 am–10 pm), so it does not offer true 24/7 flexibility. If you need a gym close to home or work, Jetts’ broader footprint gives it an edge.
list: Float Well – single Wellington CBD location, appointment‑only

sections.heading: Verdict – Which Is Right for You?
sections.body: If you value cost‑effectiveness, flexible hours and the ability to walk in for a workout, Jetts is the clear winner. It suits beginners, budget‑conscious members and anyone who wants a no‑strings‑attached gym experience. Float Well is best for athletes, frequent travellers or anyone prioritising recovery, stress relief and sleep quality over traditional strength training. Consider your primary goal: a functional gym routine → Jetts; a dedicated recovery routine → Float Well. Both can be made more affordable through the Exercise NZ subsidy, so check your eligibility before signing up.
list: Choose Jetts for: flexible, low‑cost gym access, 24/7, basic equipment
Choose Float Well for: specialised recovery, floatation therapy, wellness focus
